one-line thesis: India's **CTC / magnet-winding-wire leader** — the copper conductor that goes inside every power transformer. Riding the same T&D super-cycle; mgmt is explicit that **transformer supply is THE bottleneck** and the winding-wire chain "will still have a lot more capacity to add to keep up." Record FY26 (rev +61%, PAT +62%), unit economics rising (EBITDA/ton ₹52.5k→₹67.6k), 5–7yr qualification moat, and a long import-substitution runway (India CTC demand ~40k→100–120k MT by 2030). Copper is pass-through → **track EBITDA/ton, not %margin.**
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy — cop:
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Q4 FY26 | YoY |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **₹3,107 cr** | +61% | ₹1,018 cr | +101% |
| EBITDA | ₹190 cr | +54% | ₹56 cr | +60% |
| **EBITDA / ton** | **₹67,600** | vs ₹52,500 | **₹74,000** | vs ₹60,000 |
| PAT (record) | ₹110 cr | +62% | ₹34.5 cr | +87% |
| Volume | +21% | — | ~7,600 MT | +29% |
| Exports | ~30% of rev | — | 27% (Q4 +92% YoY) | — |
| Specialized wires | ~75% of rev (+62%) | — | +103% YoY | — |
| Debt/EBITDA | **0.39x** | from 1.21x | — | — |
> **Read margins via EBITDA/ton, not %** — reported % swings with LME copper (a direct pass-through, make-to-order; no copper price exposure). Q4 copper spike compressed reported %margin but EBITDA/ton *rose*. Gross profit/ton ₹1.12L→₹1.27L on CTC mix.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Volume growth FY27: ≥ last year's 21%** (full-year Supa capacity now available, was only partial in FY26).
- **EBITDA/ton: sustain ₹67,000–74,000** (mix- and export-dependent).
- **Exports: back toward ~40%** of revenue over a couple years (was ~30%, historically 40%).
- **Operating leverage:** kicks in *gradually after Q4 FY27* (new-capacity fixed costs absorbed first).
- **Cash flow:** FY26 operating CF negative (growth funding WC); fix via payables 25→30 days → better FY27 CF.
order book / demand model:
- No classic order book (make-to-order, 15–20 day turnaround); demand gated by **transformer-OEM ramp**.
- **Multi-year supply agreements** now being explored by large transformer clients for "predictability of supply" (same theme as Yash's 24–36mo blanket orders). KSH evaluating strategic/financial implications.
- **India CTC TAM:** FY25 ~40,000 MT → **FY27–28 ~70,000–75,000 MT** → **2030–32 ~100,000–120,000 MT**. ~1,000 MT/month was being *imported* on non-availability — now reversing.
capacity / expansion:
- **43,445 MT** at Mar-26 (≈65% specialized / 35% standard) → **~59,000 MT** after Supa Phase II (FY27; next tranche ~Q2 FY27). Peak util ~85%; new plant takes **2–3 yrs to ramp to 85%**.
- Optional **+10,000 MT** more (land/building/utilities ready at Supa) — decision pending demand.
- Q4 utilization ~70%.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **CTC (core):** >half of specialized; highest value-add; all exports are CTC to transformer cos on 4 continents.
- **Green copper backward integration** → H2 FY27 (cost efficiency).
- **PEEK insulated wires** (EV traction motors, 800V architecture): pilot end-Q2 FY27, meaningful 1.5–2 yrs out; EBITDA/ton ≈ CTC or higher. **Auto = 5–10% of the 59k MT capacity.**
- **Captive solar 4MW** (cost reduction).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Specialized EBITDA/ton ≈ **3x** standard. Mix (specialized vs standard, exports share, CTC share) is the swing factor — both grew, specialized faster.
- Weak rupee aids exports; **10% import duty + weak INR make imported CTC prohibitive** → domestic substitution.
capital allocation / balance sheet: - Sharply **deleveraged** (Debt/EBITDA 1.21→0.39x; most long-term debt cleared). WC 65–68 days, trending lower. IPO objects progressing (solar done; green copper in progress).
moat / competition:
- **5–7 year qualification barrier** for a new CTC entrant to reach 765kV/HVDC (PGCIL + each utility approves separately; entrants must start at 50/100 MVA and work up).
- 20-yr track record, integrated SPM lines (15–20 day turnaround), 120+ OEMs, >95% repeat.
- Transformer OEMs **unlikely to backward-integrate** CTC now (capacity available, complex continuous process needs order feed); globally none are backward-integrated.
risks & watch-items:
- Middle East shipment delays (~200–300 MT Q4 effect; rerouted/delivered in April) — temporary.
- Copper volatility distorts reported %margin optics (not EBITDA/ton).
- Negative operating cash flow in high-growth phase (improving via payables).
- Standard-wire growth outpacing specialized would dilute EBITDA/ton.
- New CTC capacity from existing qualified players (competitive intensity) — but qualification gates new entrants.
management quality / tone: - Clear, metrics-driven (EBITDA/ton framing), candid on cash flow and mix. Deleveraged aggressively. Conservative, demand-led capex.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The whole-chain capacity gap:** even if all announced transformer capacity lands in 3–5 yrs, the winding-wire chain "will still have a lot more capacity expansion to do" — a multi-year demand floor for KSH.
- Copper pass-through + value-addition matrix means **KSH's earnings are insulated from copper price** — only volume × EBITDA/ton matters.
- Import duty + weak INR are *structural* tailwinds turning a former import segment (~1,000 MT/mo) domestic.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · role | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transformer supply is THE bottleneck | CG Power ✅ (CGPOWER·500093 OEM) + whole winding-wire chain | — | OEM ramp gates KSH demand — High |
| CTC import substitution (~1,000 MT/mo; 10% duty + weak INR) | KSH self (KSHINTL·544664); Precision Wires ⭐ (PRECWIRE·523539) | importers of CTC | duty + INR make imports prohibitive — High |
| Whole-chain winding-wire capacity gap (multi-year) | KSH (KSHINTL·544664); Precision Wires ⭐ (PRECWIRE·523539) | — | demand floor even if all transformer capacity lands — Med |
| PEEK insulated wires for EV 800V | KSH self (KSHINTL·544664) | — | EV-traction optionality, 1.5–2 yrs out — Low |

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Third largest manufacturer of magnet winding wires in India by production capacity and the largest exporter of magnet winding wires from India by export revenues in Fiscal 2025 (CARE Report), selling under the 'KSH' brand.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Manufactures standard and specialised magnet winding wires — round/rectangular enamelled copper and aluminium wires, paper insulated rectangular copper/aluminium wires, continuously transposed conductors (CTC) and bunched paper insulated copper wires — which are critical components of transformers, motors, alternators and generators. Customers are primarily OEMs (122 customers in FY25) across power T&D, renewables, industrials, railways, data centers, automotive (EV and ICE), home appliances and refrigeration/air-conditioning end markets. Operates three facilities (combined 29,045 MT annual installed capacity as of June 30, 2025) plus a fourth at Supa whose Phase I commenced September 2025; exports to 24 countries contributed 32.70% of FY25 revenue.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- KSH Distriparks Private Limited — Group Company: Identified as Group Company per Board Materiality Policy (Promoter Group member with related-party transactions)
- KSH Infra Park 4 Private Limited — Group Company: Identified as Group Company per Board Materiality Policy (Promoter Group member with related-party transactions)
- Waterloo Industrial Park VI Private Limited — Corporate Promoter: One of the twelve Promoters
- KSH group — Promoter group conglomerate: Diversified business conglomerate with presence in logistics, infrastructure, services and distribution; promoters hold directorships in numerous KSH Infra Park / Waterloo Industrial Park entities

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Standard magnet winding wires:** Round enamelled copper magnet winding wires, Round enamelled aluminium magnet winding wires, Rectangular enamelled copper magnet winding wires, Rectangular enamelled aluminium magnet winding wires
- **Specialised magnet winding wires:** Paper insulated rectangular copper magnet winding wires, Paper insulated rectangular aluminium magnet winding wires, Continuously transposed conductors (CTC), Bunched paper insulated copper magnet winding wires

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Power - generation, transmission and distribution (power and distribution transformers)
- Renewables (windmill and hydro generators)
- Industrials (LT/HT motors, turbo generators, DG set alternators)
- Railways (loco-traction transformers, metro coach motors)
- Data centers (all types of transformers)
- Automotive EV and ICE (wiper/ABS motors, 2W/3W EV traction motors)
- Home appliances (BLDC and regular motors)
- Refrigeration and air conditioning (compressors, hermetic compressors)
- Exports: 32.70% of FY25 revenue from operations (24 countries as of June 30, 2025)

- PGCIL approval - PICC and CTC conductor for HVDC converter transformers and …

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration is a stated aim of the manufacturing expansion: IPO objects include new machinery for expansion at the Supa Facility, a rooftop solar power plant at Supa, and new machinery at Unit 2 (Chakan, Pune), intended to improve supply chain resilience, reduce raw material costs and ensure consistent availability of high-quality copper rods, a critical input for magnet wire production. Primary raw materials are copper and aluminium with enamel and paper as insulating materials, procured from a small supplier base (9-17 suppliers across periods) without long-term supplier agreements; top-10 suppliers account for 96.93%-98.91% of raw material cost. Manufacturing facilities are located close to Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Navi Mumbai) for logistics cost efficiency. Sales are largely make-to-order via purchase orders rather than long-term supply agreements, exposing the company to inventory/raw-material scheduling mismatches. Capex additions to plant and equipment were Rs 86.39 mn (FY23), Rs 258.32 mn (FY24), Rs 17.06 mn (FY25) and Rs 8.13 mn (Q1FY26), constituting 46.71%, 54.95%, 31.50% and 79.63% of total capital expenditure respectively.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Volume-led growth: magnet winding wire sales volume grew from 17,645 MT (FY23) to 23,324 MT (FY25); revenue CAGR 35.55% FY23-FY25
- EBITDA margin expansion: 4.75% (FY23) to 6.35% (FY25) and 7.21% in Q1 FY26
- Rising leverage into the IPO: Net Debt/Equity increased from 0.59x (FY23) to 1.17x (FY25); IPO proceeds earmarked for debt repayment
- Export mix ~33% of FY25 revenue, declining as a share (39.17% FY23 to 32.70% FY25) while growing in absolute terms
- Fixed asset turnover improved from 10.66x (FY23) to 15.19x (FY25) on continuous machinery investment

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Enhance capacity and market presence through the fourth manufacturing facility at Supa, Ahilyanagar — Phase I commercially operational from September 2025, Phase II expansion planned
- Continue investment in machinery and equipment to grow installed capacity (raised from 25,265 MT at March 2023 to 29,045 MT at March 2025)
- Set up a rooftop solar power plant at the Supa Facility for captive power generation
- Deleverage the balance sheet by prepaying/repaying outstanding borrowings from Fresh Issue proceeds

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Fourth manufacturing facility at Supa, Ahilyanagar (formerly Ahmednagar), Maharashtra: Phase I commenced commercial operations in September 2025 to further enhance capacity and market presence; Phase II expansion (new machinery) at Supa plus new machinery at Unit 2 in Chakan, Pune, and a rooftop solar power plant at Supa are to be funded from the Fresh Issue. Existing installed capacity was raised from 25,265 MT (March 2023) to 29,045 MT (March 2025) across three facilities in Chakan (2) and Taloja (1), all located near Jawaharlal Nehru Port for logistics efficiency.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Third largest Indian manufacturer of magnet winding wires by production capacity and largest exporter by export revenue in Fiscal 2025 (CARE Report)
- Comprehensive, diversified product suite (standard + specialised wires, CTC) enabling cross-selling across multiple end-use industries
- Large, strategically located manufacturing facilities close to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, giving cost and logistics efficiencies
- In-house development team of engineers, designers and technicians for new product/process development and cost reduction
- High entry barriers via stringent pre-qualification approvals: PGCIL, NTPC, NPCIL and RDSO product approvals for HVDC/765kV EHV applications
- Long-standing relationships with a diversified OEM customer base, domestic and global, under the 'KSH' brand; awards from Toshiba T&D, GE Power Grid Solutions and BHEL
- Track record of financial performance and consistent growth (FY23-FY25 revenue CAGR 35.55%, EBITDA CAGR 56.70%, PAT CAGR 59.83%)
- Experienced promoters (Chairman with 40+ years in magnet winding wires) and senior management actively involved in operations

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers contributed 52.54% of FY25 revenue from operations (53.97% in Q1 FY26; 58.99% in FY23); loss of or lower demand from key customers would materially hurt revenue
- Elevated and rising leverage — Net Debt/Equity rose from 0.59x (FY23) to 1.17x (FY25) and Net Debt/EBITDA to 2.85x; Rs 2,259.77 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for borrowing repayment, making deleveraging IPO-dependent
- Thin EBITDA margins typical of a conversion business — EBITDA margin of only 6.35% in FY25 (4.75% FY23) leaves limited buffer against input-cost or pricing shocks
- Export dependence and geographic demand risk — Exports were 32.70% of FY25 revenue across 24 countries; top five export countries (USA, UAE, Kuwait, Romania, Saudi Arabia) alone were 24.34% of revenue
- Manufacturing concentration in Maharashtra — All four facilities (Taloja, two at Chakan, Supa) are in Maharashtra, exposing operations to regional disruptions
- Promoter-group breadth and related-party linkages — Twelve promoters (98.40% pre-Offer holding) with directorships across a large KSH group conglomerate; KSH Distriparks and KSH Infra Park 4 identified as Group Companies due to related-party transactions
- Reliance on commissioned industry data — Industry positioning claims rest on the CARE Report, commissioned and paid for by the Company, which the DRHP itself flags as subject to inherent risks

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Commence commercial operations at Phase I of the fourth manufacturing facility at Supa, Ahilyanagar, Maharashtra, to further enhance capacity and market presence.**
- **Deploy Rs 870.17 million of Net Proceeds on purchasing and setting up new machinery for the Phase II expansion at the Supa Facility and at Unit 2 in Chakan, Pune.**
- **Purchase and set up a rooftop solar power plant for power generation at the Supa Facility using Rs 88.28 million of Net Proceeds.**
- **Prepay and/or repay, in full or in part, certain outstanding borrowings using Rs 2,259.77 million of Net Proceeds.**
- **Amount utilised for general corporate purposes shall not exceed 25% of the Gross Proceeds of the Offer.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Enhance capacity and market presence through the fourth manufacturing facility at Supa, Ahilyanagar — Phase I commercially operational from September 2025, Phase II expansion planned
- Continue investment in machinery and equipment to grow installed capacity (raised from 25,265 MT at March 2023 to 29,045 MT at March 2025)
- Set up a rooftop solar power plant at the Supa Facility for captive power generation
- Deleverage the balance sheet by prepaying/repaying outstanding borrowings from Fresh Issue proceeds
